thm-infinite-forest-vote-limit:
## Statement

Fix a finite training dataset and a classifier $h(x,\theta)$ taking values in an ordered finite class set $\mathcal C=\{c_1<\cdots<c_J\}$ with $J\ge2$. Let $\Theta_1,\Theta_2,\ldots$ be IID random elements of a measurable space $(\mathsf T,\mathcal T)$ with common law $Q$. Regard the sequence as a random element of $(\mathsf T^{\mathbb N},\mathcal T^{\otimes\mathbb N})$ and assume it is independent of a test pair $(X,Y)$ with law $P$ on $\mathcal X\times\mathcal C$. Assume $h$ is jointly measurable in $(x,\theta)$. For $j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}$ define $p_j(x)=Q\{\theta:h(x,\theta)=c_j\}$, and let

$$
m(x,y)=p_{k}(x)-\max_{j\ne k}p_j(x),\qquad y=c_k.
$$

For each $B\ge1$, let $G_B(x)$ be the class with the largest number of votes among $h(x,\Theta_1),\ldots,h(x,\Theta_B)$, choosing the least class index in a tie. Define the finite-forest conditional risk by

$$
PE_B(\Theta_{1:B})=\int_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal C}\mathbf1\{G_B(x)\ne y\}\,dP(x,y).
$$

If $P\{(x,y):m(x,y)=0\}=0$, then, almost surely with respect to the IID tree-randomization sequence,

$$
PE_B(\Theta_{1:B})\longrightarrow P\{(x,y):m(x,y)<0\}.
$$
thm-random-forest-strength-correlation-b:
## Statement

Fix a finite training dataset and a measurable classifier $h(x,\theta)$ taking values in an ordered finite class set $\mathcal C=\{c_1<\cdots<c_J\}$ with $J\ge2$. Let $Z=(X,Y)$ have test law $P$. Let $\Theta,\Theta'$ be independent randomizations with common law $Q$, and assume the pair $(\Theta,\Theta')$ is independent of $Z$. For $j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}$ define $p_j(x)=Q\{\theta:h(x,\theta)=c_j\}$. For $y=c_k$, let $\hat j(x,y)$ be the least index attaining $\max_{j\ne k}p_j(x)$, and define the limiting margin

$$
m(x,y)=p_k(x)-p_{\hat j(x,y)}(x),\qquad s=\mathbb E_P[m(Z)].
$$

Assume $s>0$. For a tree randomization $\theta$, define the raw margin $r_\theta(x,y)=\mathbf1\{h(x,\theta)=y\}-\mathbf1\{h(x,\theta)=c_{\hat j(x,y)}\}$ and $sd(\theta)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_P(r_\theta(Z))}$. Put $d=\mathbb E_Q[sd(\Theta)]$. If $d=0$, then $P\{m(Z)<0\}=0$. If $d>0$, define

$$
\rho=\frac{\mathbb E_{Q\times Q}[\operatorname{Cov}_P(r_\Theta(Z),r_{\Theta'}(Z))]}{d^2}.
$$

Then $\rho\ge0$ and

$$
P\{m(Z)<0\}\le \rho\frac{1-s^2}{s^2}.
$$

The covariance formula for $\rho$ is Breiman's weighted mean raw-margin correlation written without undefined zero-standard-deviation correlation terms.
thm-regression-forest-risk-under-unbiase:
## Statement

Fix a finite training dataset and a jointly measurable real-valued tree predictor $h(x,\theta)$. Let $Z=(X,Y)$ have test law $P$. Let $\Theta,\Theta'$ be independent randomizations with common law $Q$, assume the pair $(\Theta,\Theta')$ is independent of $Z$, and assume $\mathbb E_PY^2<\infty$ and $h(X,\Theta)\in L^2(P\times Q)$. For every allowed tree randomization $\theta$, assume $h(X,\theta)\in L^2(P)$ and $\mathbb E_PY=\mathbb E_Ph(X,\theta)$. Put $e_\theta(Z)=Y-h(X,\theta)$ and $sd(\theta)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_P(e_\theta(Z))}$. Define

$$PE^*(\mathrm{forest})=\mathbb E_P\left(Y-\mathbb E_Qh(X,\Theta)\right)^2$$

$$PE^*(\mathrm{tree})=\mathbb E_Q\mathbb E_P e_\Theta(Z)^2$$

$$d=\mathbb E_Q[sd(\Theta)]$$

If $d=0$, then both risks are zero. If $d>0$, define

$$
\rho=\frac{\mathbb E_{Q\times Q}[\operatorname{Cov}_P(e_\Theta(Z),e_{\Theta'}(Z))]}{d^2}.
$$

Then $\rho\ge0$ and

$$
PE^*(\mathrm{forest})\le\rho\,PE^*(\mathrm{tree}).
$$

The covariance formula for $\rho$ is Breiman's weighted mean residual correlation written without undefined zero-standard-deviation correlation terms.
